subject: Partial chunking & websocket timeouts causing streaming stalls - urgent
messages:
From: Lindsey Park <lindsey@acme-ai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unstable streaming - partial chunks and socket timeouts

Hi Priyom,

We started seeing repeated streaming stalls last night during our peak window (18:30-19:10 UTC). The client stream will emit a few chunks and then stop sending data; the connection remains open for ~30s and then we get a WebSocket-level timeout/504 on our side.

Symptoms:
- Partial chunk payloads where the final json fragment is missing (~12% of calls at peak).
- WebSocket keepalive stays active, but no new frames for ~20-40s before we hit our client-side timeout.
- Error rate spikes from 0.4% to 6.7% during the window; latency P95 climbs from 220ms to 1.9s.

I've attached a trace (stream_trace_0509.txt) and a screenshot of the client console. We're currently routing requests to your hosted endpoint in us-west-2.

This is blocking a customer-facing release tomorrow. Can we get an urgent triage call and a temporary mitigation (fall back to non-streaming or smaller model) while you investigate? We need an update within 4 hours.

Thanks,
Lindsey Park
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Acme AI
Attachments: stream_trace_0509.txt (text/plain), screenshot_0509.png (image/png)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lindsey Park <lindsey@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unstable streaming - partial chunks and socket timeouts

Hi Lindsey — thanks for the detailed report and the traces. I'm really sorry you hit this during a release window. We're escalating immediately.

I've looped in Neha (serving/runtime) and Marcus (CS/account lead) for a fast triage. Marcus — I'm going to schedule a 30-min call in the next 45 minutes. Neha — can you look at the traces and confirm whether this looks like chunk truncation at the kernel layer or an upstream routing issue?

We will propose two short-term mitigations:
1) Force non-streaming responses for the affected route (same model, batching) — quick toggle.
2) Route to a smaller model variant (lower token rate) that has historically shown fewer incomplete chunks under high concurrency.

I'll share a mitigation plan and schedule the call now.

— Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unstable streaming - partial chunks and socket timeouts

Priyom / Marcus — I pulled the trace. Initial read: this looks like intermittent tail-chunk drops coming out of the inference worker process. Two likely causes:

- Kernel-level preemption on long-attention steps under the current CUDA kernel selection (we saw this pattern previously on rtx-pool-5 when sequence length spikes).
- A small set of gateway proxies were returning 502/stream-truncate when chunk buffer exceeded 64KB; the backlog coincides with a spike in concurrent long-context requests from the customer's workspace.

Immediate actions I'm deploying now:
- Swap kernel selector to conservative path for the customer's fleet (est. 12–18 min to take effect).
- Enable prefix-KV cache bypass for the route to reduce per-request memory churn.
- If the above doesn't stabilize in 30m, we'll flip their route to non-streaming fallback.

I'll post logs and root-cause notes to the incident doc.

On Sun, May 9, 2027 at 09:12 AM Lindsey Park <lindsey@acme-ai.com> wrote:
> We started seeing repeated streaming stalls last night during our peak window...

— Neha
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unstable streaming - partial chunks and socket timeouts

Monica — customer is asking for an exec-level update and a credit for the incident window if we can't meet the mitigation SLA. They're on a committed Dedicated plan (DL-9876).

Proposed customer-facing ask:
- Immediate: apply non-streaming fallback and confirm <1 hour to implement.
- Short-term: kernel swap + rolling proxies (Neha recommends) and monitor for 24h.
- Commercial: offer one week of service credit or a 20% invoice credit for the impacted billing period if we confirm sustained errors >3% during the peak window.

If Monica approves, I'll prepare a one-page exec note and a DocuSign for the interim credit.

— Marcus
Customer Success Manager
From: Lindsey Park <lindsey@acme-ai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unstable streaming - partial chunks and socket timeouts

Thanks for the quick responses. We accepted the non-streaming fallback last night and it reduced visible errors; however our telemetry still shows a 2.1% rate of truncated outputs (smaller payloads returned without final chunk) and occasional latencies at P95 ~1.2s.

We have a partner demo tomorrow and need an interim SLA:
- A firm 4-hour mitigation window for any future regressions during our demo timeslot.
- A confirmation of the credit/compensation path in writing before EOD today.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call now if that helps.

Lindsey
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lindsey Park <lindsey@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unstable streaming - partial chunks and socket timeouts

Lindsey — quick update from our side and next steps.

What we did:
- Swapped kernel selector and rolled conservative kernels across the customer's dedicated pool (completed ~2027-05-09T10:18:00-07:00).
- Enabled KV bypass and reduced concurrent long-context worker allocation for their fleet.
- Flipped their endpoint to non-streaming for all high-concurrency routes as an on-call mitigation.

Observed impact:
- Truncated-output rate dropped from 6.7% -> 1.8% across the next 12 hours; error spike window P95 latency reduced to 480ms.

Commercial & execs:
- Monica approved a 7-day invoice credit; Marcus will send the DocuSign for the interim credit. Link: https://www.docusign.com/temporary/link/abc123
- We'll continue to monitor for 72 hours and provide a post-mortem with root cause analysis and a permanent mitigation plan (likely a kernel/quantization patch and additional proxy hardening).

Attachments: mitigation_plan_0510.pdf

Thanks for the patience — we'll keep you updated hourly during your demo window.

— Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
